adjudication_records.issue_text: addMembers and removeMember actions swallow AJAX failures by dropping returned promises and not handling .catch(), and addMembers never clears the input field after success

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `admin-group.js.es6`, `actions.addMembers` calls `this.get("model").addMembers(...)` but does not `return` the AJAX promise and has no error handling; likewise `actions.removeMember` triggers `self.get("model").removeMember(member)` inside the Bootbox callback without returning/propagating the promise, so any rejection is effectively unobserved by the action. Additionally, `addMembers` explicitly includes `// TODO: should clear the input` and never resets `this.get("usernames")` after a successful add, so the input remains populated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: removeMember action inside bootbox.confirm callback discards the returned promise from removeMember, silently masking AJAX failures with no error feedback to the user

adjudication.rationale: In the new `removeMember` action, the Bootbox callback calls `self.get("model").removeMember(member);` without chaining/returning the promise. While that does mean the returned `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` promise is ignored locally, the diff does not show any contract that this promise must be returned/handled, nor does it prove failures are “silently masked” (Discourse.ajax may have global error handling; the callback return value isn’t used by `bootbox.confirm`). This is more of a potential UX improvement than a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: usernames property is null-initialized but never set for existing groups

adjudication.rationale: In the updated flow, `usernames` is no longer derived from existing `members`; it’s an input-only field used for the "Add members" UI. It *is* set via two-way binding from `{{user-selector usernames=usernames ...}}` in `admin/templates/group.hbs` when an admin selects/types usernames, and `addMembers` reads that value and calls `model.addMembers(this.get("usernames"))`. For existing groups, `save` no longer uses `usernames` at all (it now calls `group.save()`), which matches the refactor that separates membership changes from saving group attributes. So the claim that it is "null-initialized but never set for existing groups" is not verifiably true from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No upper bound or positivity guard on the `limit` parameter in `groups_controller.rb` `members` action, allowing unbounded materialization of group members via large or negative limit values

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit` is taken directly from `params[:limit]` and converted with `.to_i` (`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i`) and then used in `group.users...limit(limit)`. There is no validation that `limit` is positive or capped to a sane maximum. A client can supply an extremely large `limit` (causing large queries/serialization work) or a negative value (DB-dependent: can error or be treated as effectively unbounded), so the finding is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 query per-username lookup in `admin/groups_controller.rb` `add_members` action, issuing separate SELECT and INSERT queries for each username

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The new `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` implementation does `usernames.split(",").each` and inside the loop calls `User.find_by_username(username)` for each username, which will issue one SELECT per username (N queries). It also calls `group.add(user)` per user, which typically results in per-user association writes (often INSERTs into the join table), again done one-at-a-time. This is a verifiable per-username query pattern introduced in the diff and can become a performance problem for large username lists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Extra COUNT(*) query on every pagination request in `groups_controller.rb` `members` action when `group.user_count` could be used instead to avoid a separate count query

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff adds `total = group.users.count` and then separately queries the paginated members (`group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`). That `count` will issue an additional `COUNT(*)` query on every request to `/groups/:group_id/members`, whereas the codebase already exposes a `user_count` attribute on groups (used throughout the diff) which could potentially supply the total without a separate query. This is a concrete, verifiable extra-query/performance regression introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `group.users.delete(user_id)` in `admin/groups_controller.rb` `remove_member` action may load the association unnecessarily instead of using a direct delete on the join table

adjudication.rationale: In the new `remove_member` action, `group.users.delete(user_id)` is a standard ActiveRecord association method that issues the necessary delete against the association (typically a DELETE on the join table) and does not inherently require loading the full `users` association. The proposed finding is an unverified performance micro-optimization suggestion, not a clear defect or correctness/security issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Route/controller parameter mismatch: add_members and remove_member call params.require(:group_id) but member routes provide :id, causing ActionController::ParameterMissing on every call to /admin/groups/:id/members (PUT or DELETE)
matched_golden_ids: The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. Both describe the same underlying bug: the routes supply the group identifier as `params[:id]`, but the controller/actions expect/read `params[:group_id]` (via `params.require(:group_id)`), causing the memberships endpoint to fail (e.g., ParameterMissing/broken feature).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public groups#members endpoint response shape changed from bare JSON array to object { members: [...], meta: {...} }, breaking existing API consumers that iterate the top-level array

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members, the response changed from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (which produces a top-level JSON array) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }` (a JSON object with `members` and `meta`). Any existing client code calling `/groups/:group_id/members` and iterating the top-level response as an array would break because the top-level type is no longer an array.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin create endpoint dropped the group param envelope, changing from params[:group][:name]/params[:group][:visible] to flat params[:name]/params[:visible], silently failing existing API clients

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#create` changes from reading `params[:group][:name]` / `params[:group][:visible]` (and `:usernames`) to reading flat `params[:name]` and `params[:visible]` (and no longer accepts the `group` envelope). There is no compatibility path to still accept `params[:group]`. Existing clients posting the old payload shape would result in `group.name` being set from `(params[:name] || '').strip` => empty string, causing `group.save` to fail and returning an error response. The JS client was updated accordingly (`Group#create` now posts `this.asJSON()` unwrapped), confirming an intentional but breaking API change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin update endpoint dropped the group param envelope, changing from params[:group][:alias_level] to flat params[:alias_level]

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `Admin::GroupsController#update` from reading nested `params[:group]` (`payload = params[:group]`) to reading flat params like `params[:alias_level]`/`params[:visible]`/`params[:name]`. However, this is paired with corresponding client-side changes: `Discourse.Group#asJSON` is changed from `{ group: {...} }` to a flat hash, and the admin controller now calls `group.save()`/`group.create()` (which send the new flat payload). The controller specs are also updated to send flat params. So within the diff, the parameter shape change is intentional and consistently applied, not a verifiable bug by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin update endpoint removed PATCH method routing entirely, causing routing errors for clients using PATCH /admin/groups/:id

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not remove PATCH routing for `/admin/groups/:id`. In Rails, `resources :groups` continues to generate both PATCH and PUT routes to the `update` action unless explicitly changed, and the routes.rb changes shown only add `delete/put "members"` under the admin groups resource. While the controller no longer has special PATCH-specific behavior (`request.patch?` handling and `update_patch` were removed), that would affect PATCH semantics (incremental membership changes), not cause a routing error for PATCH requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin update endpoint removed the incremental membership changes API (changes: { add: [...], delete: [...] }) entirely

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the old incremental membership update API: `update_patch` (handling `params[:changes]` for PATCH) is deleted, and `update` no longer branches on `request.patch?`. However, the change is accompanied by new dedicated endpoints/routes (`PUT /admin/groups/:group_id/members` => `add_members`, `DELETE .../members` => `remove_member`) and corresponding client-side/model changes and updated specs. This is a deliberate API refactor/replacement, not a clear defect introduced by the diff. Any backward-compatibility impact on external clients is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GET /admin/groups/:id/users admin route removed without replacement, causing 404 for any consumer hitting that URL

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `get "users"` member route under `admin/groups` in `config/routes.rb` and there is no corresponding `Admin::GroupsController#users` action shown. However, the admin UI is also changed to fetch members via `Discourse.ajax('/groups/' + name + '/members.json', ...)` (public GroupsController#members) and to modify membership via new admin routes `PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members.json`. So within the code shown, there is a clear replacement for the functionality the app uses; the claim that this necessarily causes a real 404 problem for “any consumer” is not verifiable from the diff and is speculative about external clients relying on the removed endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Discourse.Group.findMembers() no longer returns a promise when name is empty, changing from Ember.RSVP.resolve([]) to undefined, causing TypeError when .then() is chained

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Discourse.Group.findMembers()` does change its empty-name behavior from `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` to `return;` (undefined). However, all call sites shown in this diff that previously chained `.then(...)` on `findMembers()` were removed (`afterModel` hooks in both admin and group-members routes). The remaining/new call sites (`setupController`, `removeMember`, `addMembers`, pagination actions) invoke `findMembers()` without chaining `.then()`, so no TypeError from `.then` is demonstrable from this diff alone. Claiming a `.then` TypeError would require assuming other, not-shown callers still chain it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Discourse.Group removed createWithUsernames and saveWithUsernames public methods, breaking any plugin or theme code calling them

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly removes the `createWithUsernames` and `saveWithUsernames` methods from `Discourse.Group` and replaces usage in core with `create()`/`save()`. However, the claim that this "breaks any plugin or theme code" is not verifiable from the diff itself (it depends on external plugin/theme usage not shown). Within the changed code, call sites were updated, so no concrete defect is demonstrated in-repo by this finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Discourse.Group asJSON() no longer serializes usernames, preventing group creation/update from including membership in the same request

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally removes sending `usernames` inside group create/update. `Discourse.Group.asJSON()` now serializes only `name/alias_level/visible`, and the admin controller now calls `group.create()`/`group.save()` (not `createWithUsernames`/`saveWithUsernames`). Membership changes were moved to separate endpoints (`PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members.json`) via `addMembers`/`removeMember`, and the template only shows the add-members UI after the group has an `id`. Specs were updated accordingly (no longer expecting usernames on create). So while the observation is true, it is not a defect introduced by the diff; it matches the new API/UI design.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-automatic groups now silently paginated at limit 50 where previously all members were returned in one response, causing consumers to receive truncated results without warning

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the previous code only applied `limit/offset` pagination for `group.automatic?`; non-automatic groups returned the full ordered member list via `render_serialized(members.to_a, ...)`. The new code unconditionally applies `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)` for *all* groups, so callers that do not pass pagination params will now receive only the first 50 members for non-automatic groups. Although the response now includes `meta.total/limit/offset`, this is still a backwards-incompatible change that can lead to truncated results for existing consumers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `params.require(:group_id)` doesn't match the route's `:id` param in `add_members` and `remove_member` actions, causing `ActionController::ParameterMissing` and completely breaking member management in production
`addMembers` and `removeMember` in `admin-group.js.es6` swallow failures with no user feedback, leaving the user with no idea the operation failed

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `addMembers` simply calls `this.get("model").addMembers(...)` and `removeMember` calls `model.removeMember(member)` after confirmation, without any explicit `.catch`/failure handling or UI messaging in these actions. However, whether failures are truly "swallowed" with "no user feedback" is not verifiable from this diff alone because `Discourse.ajax` commonly has centralized error handling (e.g., global flash/popup) outside the shown changes. The diff proves lack of local error handling, but not that the user receives no feedback at all.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `setupController` in `admin_group_route.js` and `group-members.js.es6` calls `model.findMembers()` without returning the promise, breaking route error handling and the loading substate
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that `findMembers()` is now asynchronous and its promise isn’t being properly handled/returned from `setupController`, which can lead to the controller proceeding without member data (race condition) and also breaks Ember’s loading/error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `findMembers` in `group.js` returns `undefined` instead of a promise when the group name is empty, causing callers chaining `.then`/`.catch` to throw an error
`removeMember`/`addMembers` in `group.js` do not propagate the reload result from `findMembers()`, causing rejections to be lost and the member list to go out of sync

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`, both `removeMember` and `addMembers` do `return Discourse.ajax(...).then(function() { self.findMembers(); });`. Because the `then` callback does not `return` the `self.findMembers()` promise, the returned promise from `removeMember`/`addMembers` resolves as soon as the membership mutation request finishes, not when the reload finishes. Any rejection from `findMembers()` is also unhandled/lost to the caller. This is directly verifiable from the diff and can lead to callers thinking the operation is complete while `members/user_count/offset` have not refreshed (or failed to refresh).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `next`/`previous` actions in `admin-group.js.es6` optimistically mutate `offset` before `findMembers` resolves, with no rollback if the request fails

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `next` and `previous` actions compute a new `offset`, immediately do `group.set("offset", offset)`, and then call `group.findMembers()` (which performs an AJAX request). There is no error handling (`catch`/failure callback) to revert `offset` if the request fails. Since `currentPage`/`showingFirst`/`showingLast` are derived from `offset`, a failed request can leave the UI/controller state inconsistent (page indicators updated but `members` not refreshed). This behavior is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `members` action in `groups_controller.rb` doesn't bound `limit` or `offset`, allowing memory exhaustion/DoS via a huge limit or invalid SQL via a negative offset

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are used directly in `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no validation/clamping. A very large `limit` can cause the server to fetch and serialize an excessive number of users (potential DoS/memory/CPU pressure). Also, a negative `offset` (e.g. `-10`) will be passed through; ActiveRecord will generate `OFFSET -10`, which is invalid in PostgreSQL and can trigger a 500 error (at minimum a correctness/robustness issue). This behavior is introduced/visible in the diff where the action was changed to always paginate based on params.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `add_members` action in `admin/groups_controller.rb` doesn't strip whitespace from usernames, causing `find_by_username` to miss users with leading or trailing spaces

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and then calls `User.find_by_username(username)` without trimming `username`. If the `usernames` param contains entries like " bob" or "bob ", `find_by_username` will not match the real username, and those users will not be added. There is no `.strip` (or similar normalization) in this method, so the issue is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `update` action in `admin/groups_controller.rb` doesn't strip whitespace from the group name, bypassing the normalization applied during `create`

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#create` normalizes the group name via `(params[:name] || '').strip`, removing leading/trailing whitespace before saving. However, `Admin::GroupsController#update` assigns `group.name = params[:name] if params[:name] && !group.automatic` with no `.strip`, so an update request can persist a name with leading/trailing whitespace, bypassing the normalization used on create. This is a concrete inconsistency introduced/present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members automatic-group test passes wrong parameter (user_id: 42 instead of usernames), causing it to hit ParameterMissing exception instead of testing the automatic-group guard, leaving the guard effectively untested

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the automatic-group guard test for `add_members` is: `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1, usernames: "l77t"` and expects `422`. It supplies the required `usernames` param (not `user_id`), so it will not raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` from `params.require(:usernames)` and will proceed to (and test) the `return can_not_modify_automatic if group.automatic` branch. The proposed finding misreads the test/params shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test for updating a non-automatic group (name, alias_level, visible) through the refactored flat-param update action — the most common happy path has zero coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff refactors `Admin::GroupsController#update` to accept flat params (`params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:name]`) instead of `params[:group]` and changes behavior accordingly. In `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`, the only remaining `.update` test is for an automatic group (“ignore name change on automatic group”), and the prior non-automatic update tests (including updating name/members) were removed. There is no spec exercising the common happy path of updating a normal (non-automatic) group’s `name`, `alias_level`, and `visible` via the new flat-param API, so this behavior change has no direct test coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test for groups_controller#members response format change from bare JSON array to object with meta pagination fields, leaving a breaking API contract change undocumented by tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a bare JSON array) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }` with pagination fields. In the shown spec changes, only `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` is modified; there is no added/updated spec covering `GroupsController#members` to lock in the new response shape. So the response format change is untested in this diff, and it is a breaking contract for any consumers expecting an array.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removed edge-case tests (adding non-existent users, removing non-members, patching automatic groups 403) not replaced in the new test suite, leaving silent-ignore behavior untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the prior “incremental” update tests that covered edge cases like adding a non-existent username and removing a non-member (both previously expected to succeed silently). In the new controller code, similar silent-ignore behavior still exists: `add_members` skips usernames that don’t resolve (`if user = User.find_by_username(username)`), and `remove_member` uses `group.users.delete(user_id)` which will no-op if the user isn’t a member. The updated spec adds tests for automatic-group modification (422) and adding valid members, but does not add replacements for the non-existent-user / non-member cases, so those behaviors are now untested. However, the specific “patching automatic groups 403” case is less applicable because PATCH-based membership changes were removed entirely in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages computed property has an off-by-one bug when user_count is divisible by limit, causing an extra empty page and pagination controls that never disable on the real last page, with no JS test coverage

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` (unless `user_count == 0`). When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 100 users, limit 50), this yields 3 instead of 2. This makes `showingLast` false on the real last page (page 2), allowing `next` to advance `offset` to `user_count` (see `next` action uses `Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`), and `findMembers` then requests members with `offset == user_count`, which will return an empty page. Pagination controls then only disable on that empty page. This is a concrete off-by-one defect introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test that create no longer accepts usernames — existing API clients sending usernames will silently lose membership data with no error

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Admin::GroupsController#create` from accepting `params[:group][:usernames]` and applying it (`group.usernames = ...`) to only reading top-level `params[:name]`/`params[:visible]`, with no handling or validation of `usernames` at all. Extra params will be ignored, so a client that still sends usernames (even alongside the new top-level `name`) will get a successful create but the group will have no members added. The controller spec also removed the prior create test that asserted `usernames` were persisted and now only tests name stripping, so there’s no test coverage ensuring the old behavior errors or is migrated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member automatic-group test uses xhr :put instead of xhr :delete, not exercising the actual DELETE route mapping and giving false confidence that the route works
matched_golden_ids: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the remove_member test uses xhr :put instead of xhr :delete, so it doesn’t hit the DELETE route mapping. This is the same mismatch between the test method and the route’s required DELETE method described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members and remove_member actions use params.require(:group_id) but the member routes provide params[:id], causing ActionController::ParameterMissing 400 errors on real requests

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The client calls `/admin/groups/` + this.get('id') + `/members.json` for both add/remove, which hits the member route under `resources :groups` (i.e. `/admin/groups/:id/members`). In `config/routes.rb` the `put "members"` and `delete "members"` routes are defined inside the `resources :groups` block (not in a `collection` block), so Rails will supply `params[:id]`, not `params[:group_id]`. However `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` and `#remove_member` do `params.require(:group_id)`, which will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` on real requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages calculation uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 which gives an off-by-one error when user_count is exactly divisible by limit, should use Math.ceil instead

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1` (when `user_count != 0`). This is off-by-one when `user_count` is exactly divisible by `limit` (e.g., 100 users, limit 50 => floor(2)+1 = 3 pages, but there are only 2). A `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`-style calculation (with the existing zero guard) would avoid the extra page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers returns undefined when name is empty instead of returning a resolved promise like Ember.RSVP.resolve([]), breaking the promise contract for callers that chain .then()

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Discourse.Group#findMembers` was changed from `return Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` when `name` is empty to `return ;` (i.e., `undefined`). In the non-empty case it still returns the `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` promise. This makes the method’s return type inconsistent and can break any caller that assumes `findMembers()` always returns a thenable (the earlier code pattern used `.then(...)` on its result). Returning `undefined` instead of a resolved promise is a concrete behavioral regression introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member bypasses the group.remove(user) model API by directly calling group.users.delete(user_id), skipping any side effects or hooks and coupling controller to persistence internals

adjudication.rationale: In the new `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, membership removal is done via `group.users.delete(user_id)` (controller directly manipulating the association) rather than using the group’s membership API (`group.remove(user)`) that was used previously in `update_patch` and is symmetric with the still-used `group.add(user)` in `add_members`. This is a verifiable change in the diff that bypasses the established domain method and ties the controller to association/persistence details; if `Group#remove` has any logic/callbacks, they will not run here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: setupController fires model.findMembers() without returning or handling the promise, causing fetch failures to be silently swallowed instead of surfacing through the router's error pipeline

adjudication.rationale: In both `admin_group_route.js` and `group-members.js.es6`, the diff removes `afterModel` (which returned `model.findMembers()`), and instead calls `model.findMembers()` inside `setupController` without returning/awaiting the promise or attaching error handling. That means the route transition no longer depends on the members fetch, and any rejection from `Discourse.ajax(...)` in `Group#findMembers` will not propagate through Ember's route promise chain (so it won't trigger the router's error substates/pipeline the way a returned `afterModel` promise would).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Transient pagination and view state (limit, offset, user_count, members) is stored as model attributes on Discourse.Group, coupling the model to a specific view and causing collisions with multiple concurrent paginators

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add pagination/view state to the `Discourse.Group` model (`limit`, `offset`, `user_count`, and `members` set inside `findMembers`). However, the finding claims this will cause “collisions with multiple concurrent paginators”, which is not a concrete, verifiable defect shown by the diff. In this change, each route/controller uses a single paginator per group model instance (admin group page and group members route each call `model.findMembers()` on their own model instance). There’s no evidence in the diff of two paginators simultaneously sharing the same `Discourse.Group` object in one running app instance, and the transient fields are not included in `asJSON()` so they won’t corrupt saves. This is primarily an architectural/design concern rather than a demonstrated correctness bug introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addMembers never clears the usernames input after successful submission, leaving the input populated and allowing trivial double-add re-submission

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` and even includes a comment `// TODO: should clear the input`, but there is no code that resets/clears `usernames` (either immediately or after the AJAX call resolves). This leaves the user-selector input populated, making accidental re-submission (double-add request) possible and is a verifiable UX/correctness issue in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Template references members via implicit Ember proxy to the model instead of an explicit computed alias, making the binding fragile and vulnerable to silent behavior changes if a members property is later added to the controller
